newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower on lack of fresh leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower on lack of fresh leads.

text.p: Singapore shares ended weaker on Thursday amid a lack of fresh trading incentives, dealers said.
"This market will drift. It will take a lot to kick-start it," a dealer said. "There are no economic factors to fuel it. We will have depend on on situational and overseas factors."

After opening at a high of 2,192.14, the key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 9.90 points down at 2,182.55. Turnover was moderate at around 102 million shares, with losers outpacing gainers by 196 to 119.
Dealers expect the index to trade within 2,150-2,200.

Newly-listed Wong's Circuits, which topped the actives with 21.2 million shares, ended at US$0.995 against its issue price of US$0.88. Uraco ended flat at Singapore $0.90 (US$0.64) on 2.7 million shares.
Dealers said there was still evidence of investors nibbling at selected blue chips and lower-line stocks.
Creative and Van Der Horst led gainers, rising S$0.50 and S$0.15 respectively to S$14.00 and S$6.05.
One dealer said a weak property market and profit-taking weighed on City Developments, which eased S$0.40 to S$12.70.
Foreign tranches of Singapore Press Holdings led losers, shedding S$0.70 to S$26.20.
